design_condition: The pavilion structure consumes most of the site, leaving only narrow open-space strips along the surrounding streets and making a communal urban relationship with the existing small buildings impossible.

positive.statement: The interesting and rigorous starting point develops a world appropriate to young patients.

position.rationale: Whole elongated pavilion visibly defines the building’s identity and overall patient-oriented architectural world.

positive.statement: Beautiful views and attractive spatial and architectural moods convincingly convey the intended world.

position.target: beautiful views and attractive spatial and architectural moods
position.rationale: Architectural expression is assigned to the visible pavilion mass and its articulated roofline.

positive.statement: The underground car park can be organized very efficiently on just two levels.

position.rationale: Below-grade parking is not visible; location is constrained beneath the central pavilion footprint.

negative.statement: The full use of the existing land reserves leaves no reserve areas for future needs.

position.rationale: Limited reserve capacity is anchored to the narrow peripheral site strips around the pavilion.

negative.statement: The almost unbelievable length makes the postulated communal context with the existing small buildings impossible in urban-planning terms.

position.rationale: Top and elevation views clearly show the pavilion’s exceptionally elongated single-storey mass.

negative.statement: The qualities of the open spaces and surroundings appear limited because the site is largely consumed by the pavilion structure.

position.rationale: Open-space limitation is anchored to the thin residual strip beside the elongated footprint.

negative.statement: The external and internal access system is based on very long and functionally not always completely understandable paths.

position.rationale: Long access routes are approximated along the pavilion’s central longitudinal organization.

negative.statement: The distant public areas make daily operations very difficult.

position.rationale: Public-area distance is assigned toward a remote end of the visibly extended building.

negative.statement: Long paths in poorly lit, introverted corridors and a limited view of the outside result from the single-storey structure.

position.rationale: Interior corridors are not distinguishable; the estimate follows the pavilion’s central elongated circulation zone.

negative.statement: A large part of the treatment rooms can only be illuminated zenithally via skylights.

position.rationale: Treatment rooms are interior; their position is approximated beneath the roof and visible upper envelope.

negative.statement: The beautiful spatial atmospheres depicted in the perspectives remain limited to just a few points in the floor-plan concept.

position.target: few points in the floor-plan concept
position.rationale: Limited atmospheric quality is assigned to a representative portion of the otherwise repetitive floor-plan mass.

negative.statement: The proposed spatial structure is unsuitable due to its huge size, both in terms of urban planning and operation.

position.rationale: The sampled geometry visibly confirms a very large, elongated building scale affecting urban and operational performance.
